dog.now.why: After 'also' the modal jumps ahead of the subject (mues ich); both infinitives, verbiicho and verstecke, wait at the clause ends.

dog.past.why: No Präteritum: tense sits on hät/han, and the modals become bare infinitives (wele, müese) placed before the main verb.

dog.neg.why: 'mues nöd' means no need, like English; a ban would be 'darf nöd'. The second nöd waits after the object, just before verstecke.

dog.q.why: 'also' already inverts statements (mues ich), so the question has the same order as a statement: only the rising voice marks it.

cant.now.why: 'hid' has to be Perfekt (versteckt händ), the only past. After 'wil' the aux händ lands at the very end, behind the participle.

cant.past.why: 'couldn't' is händ ... chöne cho: tense moves to händ, the modal stays an infinitive and goes before cho. Clause two doesn't change.

cant.fut.why: No future and no 'be able to': plain present chönd plus morn does all of 'won't be able to ... tomorrow'.

cant.although.why: 'glich' is the spoken 'still/anyway' (Standard trotzdem). 'obwohl' works like 'wil': versteckt händ closes the clause.

like.now.why: LIKE is 'gern haa', a split door: hät sits second with the person ending, gern closes the sentence, Kafi sits in between.

like.neg.why: The negative switches to 'mag' and fuses 'not' into the object: kei Kafi (no coffee). 'Si hät Kafi nöd gern' also works.

like.they.why: Only hät changes, to plural händ; gern and Kafi stay as they are. 'Mini' already had the plural-looking form.

like.q.why: No 'do': the inflected half häsch jumps to the front and marks the question; gern still closes the sentence.

go.habit.why: Plain present gönd. Time comes before place, so 'jede Sunntig' sits between the verb and 'uf de Märt', the reverse of English.

go.prog.why: No progressive: same gönd as 'every Sunday'; 'jetzt grad' does the right-now work. 'am Gaa' doesn't take a destination well.

go.past.why: Perfekt is the only past: sind second, participle ggange (double g) at the very end, time and place inside the bracket.

go.fut.why: Future is present plus a time word: morn does the job of both 'will' and 'tomorrow'. 'werdet gaa' would sound like a guess.

go.neg.why: No auxiliary: nöd follows the verb and time word (gönd hüt nöd) and comes before the destination.

live.now.why: Plain present wohnt plus 'sit' (for/since) for something still true; no perfect. 'Jahr' stays singular after zwei.

live.past.why: Finished stretch goes Perfekt: hät second, gwohnt last. 'sit' becomes 'lang' after the number to mark the span as closed.

live.fut.why: No future perfect: present wohnt plus 'dänn scho' (by then already). Fronting 'Im Juni' flips the order to wohnt er.

live.q.why: Question word first, verb second (wohnsch du). The present carries the tense and 'scho' (already) stands in for 'have been'.

if.real.why: Main clause inverts and fuses: gönd mir becomes gömmer. 'will travel' is present 'go reise' with the extra go, no future.

if.unreal.why: Subjunctive hetted closes the if-clause, then würded fronts the main clause; 'go' still slips in before reise.

if.past.why: Past unreal is 'gha hetted', then 'wäred mir go reise': the go-construction uses wäred and no participle for travelled.

rain.now.why: Es stays as a dummy subject. 'take' is separable mitnää: nimm opens the order, mit closes it around 'en Schirm'.

rain.fut.why: No 'going to': present rägnet plus spöter makes the prediction, so spöter carries the door. 'es wird rägne' sounds bookish.

rain.neg.why: The negative order keeps plain nimm and puts the 'not' on the umbrella: kei Schirm (no umbrella), not 'nimm nöd'.
